finding.summary: New preview click-to-write path is authorized client-side only; the server-side gate it relies on is disabled by default
finding.evidence: This change turns the preview pane into a write surface: `onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : (line, checked) => setTaskChecked(view, line + 1, checked)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:258-260). The ONLY thing distinguishing a viewer from an editor on this path is the client-side `readOnly` boolean, which comes from `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` in packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:323 — a value the browser controls. packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:119-120 asserts the backstop ("a read-only share viewer has no write permission — the auth webhook would reject the update"), and packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:255 repeats it ("A read-only mount passes no callback"). But the enforcement point, packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105, is gated on `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` and defaults to SHADOW mode: when the flag is unset it logs `[shadow] would deny ...` and returns `{ allowed: true }`. `hasAccess` (line 200) is the code that would actually reject a viewer (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) and it is bypassed in shadow mode. Attacker chain: obtain any viewer-role share link, open the note, and issue a Yorkie `rw` update (devtools console against the attached document, or simply patch the client-side `readOnly` value) — the auth webhook returns allow and the edit persists to every collaborator. The write surface added here is new; the missing enforcement is pre-existing, which is why the comments claiming a server-side backstop are the concrete defect to fix (either flip enforcement or stop documenting an inactive gate as the guarantee).

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding reproduces in the repo. editor.ts:256-261 wires a new preview write path gated solely on the client-side `readOnly` flag (preview.ts:255/317 confirm the click listener and callback fire real edits). That flag originates from `resolved.role === "viewer"` in shared-document.tsx:323, browser-controlled. The claimed server backstop, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88 + 97-105, is gated on `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` and, when unset, logs `[shadow] would deny ...` then returns HTTP 200 `{ allowed: true, reason: 'shadow' }`, discarding the viewer denial computed at hasAccess line 200 (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`). A grep across the non-docs tree finds no config setting the flag to true (only README prose, design docs, and the spec stub), and docs/tasks/archive/2026/08/20260810-notifications-lessons.md:20 states it still defaults to false. No alternative server-side role check exists on the Yorkie write path — hasAccess is reachable only via decide(), whose deny is overridden in shadow mode. So a viewer-role share link holder can persist writes, while notes-view.tsx:119-120 and editor.ts:253-255 document a guarantee the system does not enforce. This is authorization/access control, squarely in the Security lane; no not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.

finding.summary: New list commands and setTaskChecked dispatch document mutations with no readOnly/editable check, unlike the sibling handler added in the same change
finding.evidence: `replacePrefixes` (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:207-209) and `setTaskChecked` (line 295-300) call `view.dispatch(...)` unconditionally. Neither consults `view.state.readOnly` nor `view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` — and CodeMirror's `EditorView.editable.of(false)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:413), which is what `initialize(..., readOnly)` sets for every share-link mount, only blocks DOM-originated input; it does not block programmatic transactions. The five commands are then re-exported on the public `NoteEditorAPI` (editor.ts:581-585), which `initialize` hands to any host via `onEditorReady`, read-only mounts included. The same change adds `noteCheckboxInput` (packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:24-30) which explicitly guards BOTH ways for exactly this reason, so the guard is inconsistent across the write paths introduced together. Today the only host is `NotesToolbar`, rendered solely from notes-detail.tsx:198 (always writable) and never from SharedNotesLayout, so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence low confidence. But `NotesToolbar`'s `readOnly` prop is optional and defaults to falsy (notes-toolbar.tsx:229, 252), so a future read-only host that renders the toolbar gets a fully functional write path on a document it may not write, with the engine offering no enforcement of its own.

verdict.reason: The file-level observation is literally true (list-commands.ts:213 and :306 dispatch without checking readOnly/editable), but it is not a security defect: every path that reaches those dispatches is already gated, and the enforced authorization boundary is server-side. (1) setTaskChecked's only production caller is editor.ts:258-260, which passes `undefined` for onToggleTask when readOnly, so preview.ts:255 never attaches the click handler and preview.ts:333-335 renders the checkboxes disabled; a repo-wide grep for setTaskChecked finds no other caller. (2) The five list commands are only reachable through NoteEditorAPI (editor.ts:581-585), whose only consumer is NotesToolbar, where notes-toolbar.tsx:252 (canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view") and :257 prevent the entire list button group (lines 300-334) from rendering on a read-only mount. (3) The real gate is the Yorkie auth webhook: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:164 and :200 compute needWrite = attr.verb === 'rw' and return link.role === 'editor' for anonymous share visitors, so a viewer's writes are denied server-side no matter what the browser dispatches. A client-side readOnly check inside a CodeMirror command is a UI affordance, not an access-control boundary — the same user could call view.dispatch or store.editText from the console — so its absence grants no capability an attacker lacks. The reviewer's own stated concern is a hypothetical future host, not a reachable path in this tree.
